versions.name: RXV2-0.9.838-gain-hides-a-rates-problem
versions.notes: Travel extents: when the collective gain is a long way from 100 % the page now says to check the collective rate on the Rates page first. A small rate (6° instead of 12°) is usually the real cause of too little collective, and raising the gain to hide it makes every bank with a normal rate drive the swash into its stops.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.837-reviews-keep-their-name
versions.notes: Opening a review no longer shows another model: when you switched models, the new model's first status reply was filed under the old model, and the old model's review was saved with it inside. The recorder now parks the old model first and holds a new connection's replies until the receiver has named itself. Existing reviews get their own names back at the next app launch; the rest of their details refresh at the next connection.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.836-sliders-all-rates-types
versions.notes: The Easy tuning sliders, and How agile? on the Rates page, now work with the ACTUAL and QUICKRATES rates types as well as ROTORFLIGHT. Agility moves the full-stick rate (Max Rate on those types, with Centre keeping its ratio so the curve keeps its shape); Stick feel moves expo. Betaflight, Raceflight and KISS types are still table-only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.835-throttle-setting-kept
versions.notes: The receiver's throttle channel setting now survives a restart. Since 0.9.230 it was read before the settings store was open, so every receiver booted holding channel 3 low whatever was saved.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.834-swash-stays-level
versions.notes: With the transmitter off, the swash no longer drops past full negative or hits its stops during updates, backups and restores. The receiver used to hold channel 3 low until it heard a transmitter; on Rotorflight helis channel 3 is the collective. It now holds the flight controller's own throttle channel and keeps every flight control centred. Also: an update started just after power-up waits for the receiver's WiFi instead of going over Bluetooth; the phone's background backup never runs during an update, and the receiver refuses flight-controller requests while one is being written; saving on the Transmitter channels or Receiver settings pages no longer switches flight-controller telemetry off.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.833-compare-reviews
versions.notes: Reviews showed the wrong flight: the receiver numbers flights by age, so a recorded flight 1 went stale after the next flight; the apps now store each flight by its own identity. New Compare models page: lines up your rates against another model's backup, bank by bank, and copies a bank's rates on request.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.832-rates-type-help
versions.notes: Rates page: press and hold 'Rates type' to see what it means - which formula turns the stick into rotation speed, why to leave it alone, and what the ACTUAL columns mean

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.831-no-wiggle-after-update
versions.notes: No Bluetooth-ready servo wiggle after a reboot the app caused - a firmware install or a save that restarts the receiver. On a helicopter that wiggle is the swash plate moving by itself straight after an update. A genuine power-on still wiggles.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.830-cli-can-leave
versions.notes: Leaving the command line no longer refuses itself: opening it pauses MSP, so the flight controller could not give the fresh disarmed answer the guard demanded before restarting it. The last answer before the command line opened now stands. On the page a refusal is an alert that says why, back and home stay put on a refusal instead of walking off with the command line open, and the one-shot latch that skipped every second attempt resets.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.829-untitled
versions.notes: A new board is called Untitled and its front page asks - rather than forces - you to rename it as soon as you can, with the menu working underneath. Two boards with the same name cannot be told apart, and the banner says so.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.828-list-follows-rename
versions.notes: iOS app: a board already in the model list takes the new name it advertises after a rename, instead of sitting there under the old one

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.827-rename-follows
versions.notes: iOS app: the link's own idea of the board's name follows a rename, so after renaming a freshly wiped chip the app no longer sits reconnecting to the name it knew before

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
